Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

legal adjective

to do with the law

also legal system, legal advice, legal expert, legal knowledge, legal matters, legal profession

classical

Cic. Off. 2.47: jūris scientiae
Cic. Brut. 145: jūris perītōrum ēloquentissimus

jūs, jūris n.

noun, third declension; its genitive serves for “legal”

law; in the genitive with a noun, legal: jūris scientia, legal knowledge

Latin puts the law in the genitive where English says “legal”: jūris perītus, a legal expert; jūris scientia, legal knowledge. For the law itself see law.

Other words

  • lēgitimus, lēgitima, lēgitimum — of the law, legal (of questions and terms)

    adjective · also used · classical · Quint. 3.6.72 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. legal (related to law or the legal system)

    In this sense post-Augustan (Lewis & Short); classically “lawful” (see legal, allowed by law).

  • lēgālis, lēgāle — of the law, legal

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 3.5.4: lēgāle genus; M-O s.v. legal (related to law or the legal system)

    Quintilian’s term for the kind of question that turns on written law; post-Augustan and rare.

  • forēnsis, forēnse — of the courts and public business

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 170: ōrātiō jūdiciālis et forēnsis (Lewis & Short)

    Of the forum, where the courts sat: what belongs to a lawyer’s work and public life.

Examples

  • ut ēloquentium jūris perītissimus Crassus, jūris perītōrum ēloquentissimus Scaevola putārētur

    so that Crassus was held the best lawyer among the orators, and Scaevola the best orator among the lawyersCic. Brut. 145

See also law, legal, case, judge.
